finding.not_missing: A second planner, generic neural decoder, model weights, or a proof authority boolean is not required to add this bounded planning/admission join.

phase_1.authority: Nomination receipt and decoder output grant no permission. Native signed admission grants administrative scheduling permission; validation, claims, publication and completion remain separate owner gates.
phase_1.bindings: Unique operation/task IDs; exact native matchers retained by existing validator; disjoint declared output subsets whose union equals the generic profile outputs; exact requirement/operation/task dependency mapping; task-specific validation and acceptance keys.
phase_1.commands: Shared runtime canonical producer builds one fixed structural-smoke selector per task with exact bounded argv; no candidate execution, arbitrary validator injection or hidden benchmark verifier exposure.
phase_1.declaration: Opt-in terminal-public-task-profile@2 with <=16 exact task-to-operation bindings, instruction hash and requirement-contract CID. Preserve @1 bytes, smoke and default path.
phase_1.existing_refusals: Do not lift multi-task context, START, Doctor wrapper, candidate-runner or published-refresh refusals in this first increment.
phase_1.preparation: Sign all canonical specs with the existing active local profile; set max_tasks to the declared bounded count; store an explicit versioned prepared spec list; reconstruct equality before selection and admission.
phase_1.required_contract: Explicit intent-plan-requirement-contract@2 for the complete original public instruction. Atomic mandatory requirements only; reject unresolved source units and unsupported compounds; no direct/provider fallback.
phase_1.reuse_join: build_intent_symbolic_plan -> local.admit_local_benchmark_plan -> local.materialize_local_benchmark_plan, with existing signature/source/profile checks, deterministic replay and owner transaction.
phase_1.scope: Reviewed generic decomposition through planning and native administrative materialization only.

phase_2.invalidation: Completed task changes must create an explicitly verified source successor and refresh dependent context before it becomes executable; stale task/world/source/model selection refuses.
phase_2.reuse: Reuse exact signed raw source inventory and frozen embedding/index/checkpoint identities; bind each task CID/revision/alias/plan and dependencies to its own native owner world context.
phase_2.scope: Per-task context and source-currentness across dependency waves.

phase_3.qualification: Qualify dependency-aware readiness, isolated parallel independent tasks and restart recovery before claiming parallel benchmark execution.
phase_3.reuse: Use an explicit native multi-task execution scope following existing finite/inventory owner controls; preserve lease/worktree isolation, exact effects, validation, independent review, merge currentness and durable completion gates.

priority_row.capability: Symbolic decomposition in generic benchmark profiles

negative_controls: dropped, added, duplicated, reversed or cyclic task/operation dependencies
missing/extra/wrong effect or media type, overlapping task output ownership
unresolved source or unsupported compound requirement
forged accepted/proof/execution/completion flags and owner-resigned selection receipt
source drift during transactional materialization rolls back complete task population
fake native owner, mutated native row or dependency edge before owner verification
@2 context or START rejects until per-task execution scope is qualified
recommended_validation.new_parallel_positive: Two independent operations produce one symbolic wave with two tasks; retain administrative-only scope and no concurrency/success claim.
recommended_validation.new_positive: Generic @2 profile with two independently authored atomic requirements and two disjoint outputs, one dependency edge; actual prepare -> symbolic compiler/critic/formal validator -> signed admission -> transactional IntentRepository materialization -> real Quack owner task/contract/dependency verification. Zero provider calls or training.
